facts.text: The Centerfold Girls shot in just 21 days in December 1973 on a reported budget of $181,000, on 16mm film.
The actress playing the first victim on the beach was reportedly a real-life stripper.
Star Andrew Prine suggested his killer, Clement Dunne, wear all black and live in an all-white bedroom, to show Dunne sees the world in black and white.
Director John Peyser mostly worked in TV. He also directed episodes of The Rat Patrol and The Man from U.N.C.L.E.
Opening on a killer burying a victim on a beach, the film anticipates Maniac (1980), according to JA Kerswell of Hysteria Lives.
Jaime Lyn Bauer (Jackie) was Miss Phoenix and won the swimsuit portion of the 1968 Miss Illinois pageant, before becoming a soap star on The Young and the Restless.
Jaime Lyn Bauer appeared in 1,556 episodes of The Young and the Restless and 523 of Days of Our Lives.
Aldo Ray, who plays motel owner Ed Walker, was a former Navy frogman whose raspy voice made an officer call him 'the first frogman who sounded like one.'
Aldo Ray was once elected Constable of Contra Costa County, CA at age 23, beating the incumbent by 500 votes.
Jennifer Ashley (Charly) hated making this film. It was her first major role, and her first nude scenes left her mortified at the crew staring.
Ruthy Ross, who plays Glory, was the real June 1973 Playboy Playmate of the Month, a fitting casting for a film about centerfold models.
Francine York (Melissa) later played Marilyn Monroe in Marilyn Alive and Behind Bars, a segment in the film Night Train to Terror.
Jennifer Ashley (Charly) told The Oak Drive-In she was uneasy about the nudity but decided it came out well. She added that a lot of her fan mail comes from prison inmates.
Francine York said she clashed with co-star Ray Danton on set. Since their characters were supposed to fight, it made their arguing scenes easier.
Janet Wood (Linda) shares her name with Joyce DeWitt's character on Three's Company, which debuted two years later. Wood later guest-starred on the show.
Hippies who call themselves 'the family' and their cabin 'the ranch' are, per JA Kerswell of Hysteria Lives, a nod to the Manson clan.
The film is an anthology in three linked segments, like an Amicus horror film, with Andrew Prine's killer tying the stories together.
Abroad it got blunt retitling: Italy called it Troppo nude per vivere ("Too Naked to Live"), and Germany called it Der Rasiermesserkiller ("The Razor Killer").
Mike Mazurki, who plays the caretaker, was a Ukrainian-born law graduate turned pro wrestler and Mae West's bodyguard. He later appeared in a Rod Stewart video.
Screenwriter Bob Peete later wrote for TV's Good Times. Story co-credit Arthur Marks worked on Bonnie's Kids and Friday Foster.
Story co-credit Arthur Marks directed 76 episodes of TV's Perry Mason, then founded General Film Corporation to feed drive-ins, the market the major studios were ignoring.
The film's tagline: 'The most beautiful girls in the world! He was their JUDGE... JURY... and EXECUTIONER!'
Arthur Marks, who conceived this film's story, also directed the Detroit 9000 (1973), a hit that Quentin Tarantino brought back to theaters in 1998.
Dennis Olivieri (Tim), billed as Dennis Joel, was a child actor and singer who also appeared in Phantom of the Paradise (1974).
Ray Danton (Perry Sutton) made his name playing gangster Legs Diamond in The Rise and Fall of Legs Diamond (1960). He married actress Julie Adams, and the marriage lasted until 1981.
Most killings are obscured and shown mostly through blood splatter. Hysteria Lives counts nine deaths, mostly throat cuttings with a straight razor.
Jeremy Slate, who plays the ineffectual police detective, was in John Wayne's The Sons of Katie Elder (1965) and Wayne's True Grit (1969), and he wrote lyrics for Tex Ritter.
Andrew Prine went straight from this film to a villain role on TV's Wonder Woman, according to Hysteria Lives.
The Retro Slashers blog says each story has its own flavor: the first resembles a Russ Meyer film and the second plays like an Italian giallo.
Aldo Ray later turned up in more slashers: Haunts (1977), Straight Jacket (1982) and Terror Night (1987).
Mike's Take on the Movies suggests the film's multi-story structure and victims who turn the tables may have influenced Quentin Tarantino's Death Proof.
The film is also known as Girl Hunter. Troma Entertainment, founded in 1974, later became its home-video distributor.
Andrew Prine (killer Clement Dunne) was in John Wayne's Chisum (1970) and later starred in the killer-bear movie Grizzly (1976).
Tiffany Bolling also starred in Wicked, Wicked (1973), and later battled spiders opposite William Shatner in Kingdom of the Spiders (1977).
Ray Danton later became a director: he made Deathmaster (1972) and Psychic Killer (1975), then directed many episodes of Magnum, P.I.
Tiffany Bolling said her primal scream was real: frustrated at being stuck in low-budget schlock, she let all her pent-up anger out.
The final fight takes place in a forest left skeletal by a real fire, which broke out at the Topanga Canyon location during the shoot.
The Retro Slashers blog argues the film can be read as feminist horror, since viewers sympathize with the women while most of the men are predators.
JA Kerswell of Hysteria Lives called the film 'an excellent slice of the sick, sick 70s.'
